canonical_serializable_summary.encoding: Canonical JSON object with fixed field names; defect list sorted ascending by (anchor_position,guard_rank,guard_code); booleans encoded as JSON true/false; missing boundary operands encoded as explicit null; no map-order or evaluator-order semantics.

fields.defects: deduplicated finite ordered list of defined rejecting defects, each {anchor_position,guard_rank,guard_code}; details not needed for verdict identity may be stored separately but cannot change key order
fields.first_rejection: null iff defects empty, else defects[0]
fields.fail_seen: OR of all semantically admissible H_d fail evidence seen so far
fields.unknown_seen: OR of all retained UNKNOWN-barrier evidence seen so far
fields.tail: boundary interface of the immediately preceding input row with explicit definedness for ordinal,event_class,q_after, sufficient for G_order/G_chain against the next row
fields.terminal_q: latest defined semantic q state after schema-complete semantically admissible transitions; null only before any such state exists

canonical_serializable_summary.invariant: first_rejection equals min(defects) under the fixed total key order; fail_seen and unknown_seen are monotone; tail describes the last consumed input position rather than the last valid row.

deterministic_extend_transition.step_1_schema: Increment rows_seen. Evaluate G_schema first and emit its defined defect key at the current input anchor when malformed; undefined row-local predicates are suppressed, not guessed.
deterministic_extend_transition.step_2_pairwise: Using S.tail and the new row's defined operands, evaluate exactly the defined G_order and G_chain predicates. Any cross-boundary defect anchors at the new row position.
deterministic_extend_transition.step_3_local: For schema-complete operands evaluate G_monotone, G_class and G_nuisance plus the existing semantic/control predicates G_unknown_barrier, G_deferred_kind and G_fail_continue under the predecessor guard model.
deterministic_extend_transition.step_4_semantics: Set fail_seen'=S.fail_seen OR new_fail_evidence and unknown_seen'=S.unknown_seen OR new_unknown_evidence. Update terminal_q only through a schema-complete semantically admissible transition; never clear already observed fail/unknown evidence.
deterministic_extend_transition.step_5_defects: Union the new defined defect keys with S.defects, canonical-sort/deduplicate, and set first_rejection' to the first element or null. Existing earlier keys cannot be displaced by later anchors.
deterministic_extend_transition.step_6_boundary: Set tail to the new row's boundary interface with explicit null/definedness, even when the row is malformed, so the next append reproduces batch-defined pairwise predicate availability.
deterministic_extend_transition.step_7_outcome: Compute diagnostic VALID iff defects' empty else INVALID(first_rejection'); semantic FAIL iff fail_seen', else UNKNOWN iff unknown_seen', else PASS iff terminal_q' has b&r&f&s, else UNRESOLVED; accepted iff VALID and PASS.

inductive_equivalence_proof.theorem: For every finite trace in the predecessor V0-V9/C0-C4 verifier scope, folding extend from the empty canonical summary yields the same rejecting defect set and canonical first_rejection, fail_seen, unknown_seen, terminal_q, and diagnostic/semantic outcome as complete batch scanning with the same guard predicates and anchor/rank rules.
inductive_equivalence_proof.base_case: For the empty trace both procedures have rows_seen=0, defects=[], first_rejection=null, fail_seen=false, unknown_seen=false, tail=null, terminal_q=null, diagnostic VALID and semantic UNRESOLVED.
inductive_equivalence_proof.induction_hypothesis: Assume incremental summary I(P) equals batch summary B(P) on all verifier-observable components after prefix P.
inductive_equivalence_proof.induction_step: For appended row x, every newly evaluable predicate is either row-local on x or pairwise between the immediately preceding input row and x. I(P).tail equals the batch predecessor boundary by hypothesis, so both procedures evaluate the same defined G_order/G_chain predicates; both evaluate the same schema/local predicates on x; both OR the same new fail/unknown evidence; both apply the same admissible q transition; and both union the same newly anchored defect keys. Canonical min therefore gives the same first_rejection. Thus I(P·x)=B(P·x).
inductive_equivalence_proof.corollary_vectors: Because V0-V9 and C0-C4 are finite traces inside this guard model, the theorem applies to each without special cases: schema/order/chain/monotone/class/nuisance defects, UNKNOWN retention, deferred states, fail-continue behavior, equality, undefined operands, same-anchor ties, anchor-over-rank precedence, and reject-does-not-hide-fail are preserved exactly.
inductive_equivalence_proof.crash_resume_relevance: The summary is a sufficient deterministic fold state: serializing it after any prefix and resuming extend on the remaining suffix is observationally equivalent to uninterrupted batch scanning for the tested verifier observables. This proves resume equivalence only for the verifier computation, not for arbitrary external side effects.
